title: Ideal membership is detected at all maximal localizations
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J$ an ideal of $A$, and $a\in A$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ let $A_{\mathfrak m}$ be its prime localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $JA_{\mathfrak m}$ the ideal generated by the image of $J$. If $a/1\in JA_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, then $a\in J$.

source.place: Lemma 10.23.1 (00HN), part (1), applied to the class of a in A/J; exact Mathlib specialization Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal.

proof.text: If $a\notin J$, the ideal $K=\{s\in A:sa\in J\}$ is proper. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Membership $a/1\in JA_{\mathfrak m}$ supplies $s\notin\mathfrak m$ with $sa\in J$, hence $s\in K\subseteq\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. The zero ring case is automatic since it has only the unit ideal. Mathlib Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal states exactly this implication.

proof_origin.place: Proof of part (1), the annihilator of an element of A/J.

mathlib_searches.query: ideal membership detected by all maximal localizations of commutative ring

mathlib_searches.results: Exact match in Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalProperties.Basic; works already for commutative semirings.

mathlib_match.how: Exact implication for CommSemiring A, hence for CommRing A, arbitrary ideal J and element a.

from.place: Conormal freeness in the finite-etale-lifting route: the 00HN local-to-global step of 00SV (3), formulated for coefficient membership.

lean.statement: theorem Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] {r : R} {J : Ideal R} (h : ∀ (P : Ideal R) (_ : P.IsMaximal), algebraMap R _ r ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime P)) J) : r ∈ J
